ledger.title: Glottolog 5.3
ledger.creators: Hammarström, Harald; Forkel, Robert; Haspelmath, Martin; Bank, Sebastian
ledger.attribution: Glottolog 5.3 — Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank (2026), Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. CC-BY-4.0.
ledger.layer: the language spine: glottocode, family, coordinates, vitality, attestation
ledger.note: 7,674 spoken-L1 languages of 8,618 language-level languoids; 7,672 with coordinates. Filtered on `category`, never on `Level` — see A6.

ledger.title: Glottography
ledger.creators: Ranacher, Peter; Forkel, Robert; Efrat-Kowalsky, Nour; Urban, Matthias; and the Glottography contributors
ledger.attribution: Glottography — Ranacher, Forkel, Efrat-Kowalsky, Urban et al., Scientific Data 12:1466 (2025). CC-BY-4.0, 26 component datasets.
ledger.layer: language areas — the polygons the language field is rasterised from
ledger.note: 26 of 29 dataset repositories. THREE ARE CC-BY-NC AND EXCLUDED — bowern2021australia, haynie2019modern, wurm1981pacific — against the collection paper's own blanket CC-BY claim. The gate reads licence text, because GitHub's licence API returns NOASSERTION for all three.

ledger.title: ETOPO1 Ice Surface, 1 arc-minute
ledger.creators: Amante, Christopher; Eakins, Barry W. — NOAA NGDC
ledger.attribution: ETOPO1 1 Arc-Minute Global Relief Model — Amante & Eakins (2009), NOAA National Geophysical Data Center. Public domain.
ledger.layer: elevation and bathymetry — the substrate the whole surface is lit from
ledger.note: US federal work, no licence required. 10800×21600 int16, ice surface.

ledger.title: GHS-POP R2023A, 2020 epoch, 30 arcsec
ledger.creators: Schiavina, Marcello; Freire, Sergio; MacManus, Kytt — European Commission JRC
ledger.attribution: GHS-POP R2023A — Schiavina, Freire & MacManus (2023), European Commission Joint Research Centre. CC-BY-4.0.
ledger.layer: speaker density — the luminance channel of the language field
ledger.note: The WGS84 (EPSG:4326) product, NOT the Mollweide one — which is why no reprojection is exercised in this build. Placed by its own geotransform: it spans 178.20° of latitude, not 180, and assuming 180 put 70 people/km² on Everest's summit and lost 340 million people.

ledger.title: Ecoregions 2017
ledger.creators: Dinerstein, Eric; Olson, David; Joshi, Anup; Vynne, Carly; Burgess, Neil D.; et al. — RESOLVE
ledger.attribution: Ecoregions 2017 © RESOLVE — Dinerstein et al., "An Ecoregion-Based Approach to Protecting Half the Terrestrial Realm", BioScience 67(6): 534–545 (2017). CC-BY-4.0.
ledger.layer: biome — the land material, and the project's current proxy for growing season
ledger.note: 847 ecoregions, 14 biomes + rock/ice. Keyed on the shapefile's own BIOME_NUM, never on a re-derived index — a remap disagreeing with its own label array is how the Sahara came to report itself as 'ice, rock or water'. ⚠ Biome is a PROXY for growing season, not growing season: register item C3.

ledger.title: MOD13C2 NDVI, monthly CMG, 2024
ledger.creators: Didan, Kamel — NASA LP DAAC / MODIS Land Science Team
ledger.attribution: MOD13C2 Vegetation Indices — Didan (2024), NASA LP DAAC, via NASA Earth Observations. Public domain.
ledger.layer: greenness — PEAK NDVI over the year, the land's tone
ledger.note: Peak, not annual mean: the mean is dominated by the months boreal forest is under snow, so taiga scored like semi-desert. ⚠ NOT the AVHRR_CLIM_M product, which reads like a vegetation climatology and is sea surface temperature — it was wired in first and saturated the whole land surface.

ledger.title: MOD10C1 snow cover, monthly, 2020
ledger.creators: Hall, Dorothy K.; Riggs, George A. — NASA NSIDC DAAC
ledger.attribution: MOD10C1 Snow Cover — Hall & Riggs (2020), NASA NSIDC DAAC, via NASA Earth Observations. Public domain.
ledger.layer: snow cover — a measured snowline rather than an invented height threshold
ledger.note: Annual mean, not peak: peak snow is 100% anywhere it ever snows, which would put permanent ice on Warsaw.

ledger.title: Wikidata native labels (P1705) and writing systems (P282)
ledger.attribution: Wikidata (CC0), properties P1394, P1705, P282, P218, P220.
ledger.layer: AUTONYMS — what a language's own speakers call it, in its own script
ledger.note: Register D6. Joined on P1394 (glottocode, our own key) with P220 (ISO 639-3) as the alias fallback. Covers 1,089 of 7,672 languages — partial, and the card says so rather than passing an exonym off as an autonym.

ledger.title: UDHR in XML
ledger.attribution: Universal Declaration of Human Rights translations, UDHR in XML (E. Muller).
ledger.layer: parallel prose — Article 1 of the UDHR in 432 languages and 38 scripts
ledger.note: 446 distinct languages, 49 scripts. HAS NO LICENCE FILE. Ships only under the user's recorded decision SCOPE §12 D2, behind a single feature flag so it is removable in one commit, with per-block provenance and a takedown path. An email to the maintainer is register item F1.

ledger.title: ASJP — Automated Similarity Judgment Program
ledger.creators: Wichmann, Søren; Holman, Eric W.; Brown, Cecil H. (eds.)
ledger.attribution: ASJP — Wichmann, Holman & Brown (eds.), Automated Similarity Judgment Program, via the Lexibank CLDF edition. CC-BY-4.0.
ledger.layer: the word tier — ASJP's core 40 concepts for 6,110 languages
ledger.note: 380,912 forms. Joined on Glottocode, which is ASJP's own key. Forms are in **ASJPcode**, a deliberately coarse ASCII transcription for cross-language comparison — NOT the language's own orthography, and the card says so. ASJP marks its core 40 with a leading asterisk in the concept name; matching without stripping it found 4 concepts of 100 and produced an empty file.

ledger.title: Wikimedia Commons — manuscripts, inscriptions and objects
ledger.creators: Wikimedia Commons contributors and the holding institutions
ledger.licence: mixed-open (public domain, CC0, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA; per file)
ledger.attribution: Wikimedia Commons — each image carries its own licence, title and author, shown on the exhibit beside it.
ledger.layer: the gallery (26 objects) and the spoken recordings (15, Lingua Libre)
ledger.note: Admitted by MACHINE, per file, on the licence Commons reports for that file: public domain, CC0, CC-BY and CC-BY-SA pass; NonCommercial, NoDerivatives and fair-use fail. A public-domain manuscript can carry a restrictively licensed photograph, so the object's age is never the test. This is the same per-file gate register D3 specifies for audio, built for images first.

ledger.title: Phlorest — dated language phylogenies
ledger.creators: Forkel, Robert; Greenhill, Simon J.; and the original study authors
ledger.attribution: Phlorest — Forkel & Greenhill (eds.), a CLDF collection of published Bayesian language phylogenies. CC-BY-4.0, per-study citations in each dataset.
ledger.layer: root ages — the only real time depth in the genealogy view
ledger.note: 19 families dated of 30 datasets; 11 rejected. **Do not trust the scaling field**: one tree's stated unit gives a 613,594-year root, and four are scaled in substitutions or 'change', which are not time at all. Every age is bounded to 300-12,000 years and two have an inferred unit, marked as such in the app.

ledger.title: PHOIBLE 2.0
ledger.attribution: PHOIBLE 2.0 — Moran & McCloy (eds.), 2019, Max Planck Institute for the Science of Human History. CC-BY-SA-3.0.
ledger.note: ShareAlike, and therefore the first source that makes SCOPE §12 D3 bite: the moment this is ingested, our emitted phonology data inherits SA.
